sanskrit_verse: त्रिरात्रोपोषितो जप्त्वा ब्रह्महा त्वघमर्षणम् । अन्तर्जले विशुद्ध्येत दत्त्वा गां च पयस्विनाम् ॥
transliteration: trirātropoṣito japtvā brahmahā tv aghamarṣaṇam | antarjale viśudhyeta dattvā gāṃ ca payasvinām ||
sph_interpretive_translation: One who has committed the sin of killing a Brahmin, after observing a fast for three nights and performing prescribed mantras, becomes purified by offering cows yielding milk to qualified recipients.
jurisprudential_principles: Authority resides in ritual action performed with intent
Causation arises through sequential purification, not punishment
Capacity-based responsibility is restored through dharmic offering
Restoration logic operates via completion and conscious re-alignment
Consciousness alignment occurs through sacrificial giving
executable_legal_axioms: IF actor commits brahmahatya THEN initiate triratra uposana protocol
IF uposana completed AND mantra recitation verified THEN proceed to gau danam
IF gau danam executed to eligible recipient THEN declare consciousness realignment
IF any step uncompleted THEN defer judgment until full restoration sequence enacted
supreme_court_application: In adjudicating acts of grave spiritual misconduct, the court must recognize that restoration supersedes punitive measures. The accused's eligibility for reintegration depends upon enactment of the complete purification sequence under supervision of competent dharmic authority.
nyaya_and_non_punitive_alignment: Pramāṇa lies in observance and offering, not infliction. Anupūrvaśaḥ governs the process: first restraint, then invocation, finally donation. Responsibility aligns proportionally with capacity to restore balance. Non-punitive reality rule confirms that suffering is irrelevant where consciousness is cleansed.
restorative_enforcement_protocols: Verify Mantra Recitation Accuracy Through Vedic Auditor
Execute Gau Danam Under Qualified Recipient Validation
Confirm Consciousness Realignment Through Post-Offering Assessment
final_declaration: By the Source-Authority of the Supreme Pontiff of Hinduism, Bhagavan Nithyananda Paramashivam, this law stands established: Dharma prevails through purification, not punishment; reality remains non-retaliatory; consciousness alone adjudicates truth.
